correctness.rationale: For every finite alphabet product, support-cardinality/lex ordering and deletion of the largest-index nonzero coordinate give ancestor-closed prefixes, commuting retractions, and a two-case edge estimate Lip≤2. The penultimate retraction has Lip≥2 outside n=1 and binary n=2 via the full neighbor-ball obstruction; explicit nonexpansive chains cover exceptions. The graph path metric promotes all edge estimates to every pair, and canonical free-space linearization proves the stated separate bound without claiming optimality for unrestricted linear bases. The supplemental checker validates finite instances and is not used for the all-dimensions quantifier.

value.rationale: The invariant is motivated directly by dimension-uniform but nonoptimal retractional basis constructions for Lipschitz-free spaces. A single sharp uniform constant across every finite heterogeneous Hamming box and a complete isolated nonexpansive-exception classification provide structural information beyond isolated computations: a support-ancestor construction and a universal last-stage neighborhood obstruction explain both threshold and exception. These are useful benchmarks for quantitative finite metric free-space bases. No downstream optimal unrestricted Schauder basis is claimed.
